Separate, lower-priority topic split out of #172.

## Goal

Define, in Adashi design, how a plugin can contribute **workflow nodes** (custom nodes) — the original Aworkit motivation for plugins. This is a **later feature**; this task produces the design decision, not the implementation.

## To decide and record

- Contribution kinds a manifest may declare beyond tools (node, provider, evaluator, adapter) and the exact descriptor for a workflow node (ports, input/output schema, configuration schema, execution semantics).
- The host protocol: reuse MCP where it fits (MCP already has tools/prompts/resources; node execution is not MCP) vs the native `PluginHandshakeV1` subprocess protocol already sketched in the trusted-extension design. Decide honestly, including whether a node is just a tool with a fixed port shape.
- Identity, version/hash pinning, enablement, trust, and side-effect hints inherited from the tool-plugin work.
- How a custom node appears in the workflow editor and validates, freezes, and executes.
- Authority/approval/secret-lease path for node execution; failure/degraded and uncertain-effect semantics.
- Removal/update semantics consistent with #172 (a missing node must not stop an existing workflow; the model is told it is missing).

## Relationship

Depends conceptually on #172 (Codex-shaped tool plugins, folder, trust, enablement). The trusted-extension registry and native protocol currently deferred there are the starting material for this design.

data.title: Design workflow node plugins (custom nodes) and record the decision in Adashi (later feature)
